ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against: Global Affairs Canada Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) sanctions lists; Canadian Criminal Code Part II.1 terrorism financing lists; UN Security Council Consolidated List; US OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identification lists; FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists. Screening must be performed at initiation, before signing, and repeated within 24 hours prior to filing; negative PEP hits and sanctions matches are reported to FINTRAC under STR requirements. All results must be retained for 10 years per PCPMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online transaction portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca) with NUANS name search via authorized service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names in Quebec must comply with the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11); the name must be in French unless expressly permitted by the REQ (e.g., a recognized trademark or a French version is not feasible). Latin-script transliteration is used for foreign names; accents and French characters are mandatory for statutory French-language names. No non-Latin scripts are accepted in the legal name except as a transliterated French or English form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the REQ rejects a name, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registraire within 30 days of notification, providing prior PTO/trademark registrations, photocopies of trademark searches, and explanations of distinctive elements. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec (TAQ) under the ARLPE, ss. 26-27. A fresh name reservation must be obtained if the initial 90-day window expires; only one 30-day extension is available upon payment of the statutory renewal fee and justification of ongoing use.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are acceptable for the statutory registered office in Quebec under QBCA s. 36, provided a natural person resident in Quebec is designated as the registered agent and the address is a physical street address (not a P.O. box) at which process can be served during normal business hours. However, for a hardware AI toy manufacturer targeting a low-risk AML tier, the CRA and Quebec Revenu consider the absence of actual inventory storage or operational presence to be a red flag for permanent establishment; therefore a commercial substance arrangement (e.g., a shared warehousing or fulfilment contract in Quebec) is strongly recommended. Virtual office for registered office only: 35% fatigue factor; not for manufacturing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c S-31.1 (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), ss. 8 (articles), 9 (incorporation), 12 (first directors), 27 (registered office), 61 (board of directors); supplemented by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1. Optional federal regime: Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Québec Enterprise Registrar — Registre des entreprises du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed electronically together with the Declaration of Incorporation (déclaration d'immatriculation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors may determine (QBCA s. 28). Initial paid-up capital is set by the first board resolution and recorded in the share register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the incorporation of the Corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Québec) is ratified; the incorporator's subscription for 1,000 common shares at $1.00 per share is accepted and recorded in the securities register; (2) the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [registered office address], Province of Québec, and the minute book, share register and corporate records are maintained at that address; (3) [President Name] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, and [Secretary-Treasurer Name] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer, each to hold office until the next annual meeting; (4) the proposed by-law No. 1 is adopted; and the officers are instructed to complete all public filings, open corporate bank accounts and take all ancillary actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and NUANS Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Online Name Reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search against the Quebec Enterprise Register and the federal trade-marks database; submit the online name reservation application indicating the head office jurisdiction (Quebec) and the proposed name in French and/or English; pay the $35 CAD reservation duty; retain the reservation certificate, valid for 120 days, for use in the articles.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in French and English variants
NUANS name search report
Full legal name, address and signature of incorporator
Quebec head office address declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, prepare a revised distinctive element and file a new reservation within the validity period; request a clerical reconsideration by REQ if the refusal is based on an erroneous register match.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — authenticated electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles under s. 8 QBCA specifying corporate name, share classes and any restrictions on share transfers, and the number of first directors; execute the articles by the incorporator with a declaration of incorporation; where the entity's finance partners so require, procure a certified copy notarized before a Quebec notary or commissioner of oaths.
required_dossiers: Statutory form of articles of incorporation (statuts constitutifs)
Certificate of name reservation issued by REQ
Consent of each first director to act (s. 17 QBCA)
Declaration of incorporation (déclaration d'immatriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: REQ issues a notice of deficiency; respond within 15 days with amended articles, or withdraw the filing with a refund request; all corrections are made electronically through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing, Certificate of Incorporation and NEQ Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Registre des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed articles together with the declaration of incorporation and statutory duties (approximately $337 CAD for an extra-provincial/provincial corporation); upon registration, REQ issues the certificate of incorporation and assigns the Numéro d'entreprise du Québec (NEQ); thereafter obtain the federal 9-digit Business Number from the Canada Revenue Agency via Business Registration Online (BRO).
required_dossiers: Executed articles of incorporation
Declaration of incorporation
Proof of payment of incorporation duties
Certificate of name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed, contact REQ's inspection and correction service; rectify any suspended registration under s. 40 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and file the missing declaration within the prescribed delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration (GST/HST, QST, Corporate and Payroll Accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec — Entreprises Québec online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enrol with the CRA through BRO for a Business Number (BN), the GST/HST account (RT), payroll deductions account (RP), and import-export account (RM) if applicable; simultaneously register with Revenu Québec for QST (RM), provincial corporate income tax (RC) and provincial payroll source deductions (AS); file the beneficial ownership information register as required for the corporate record and disclose to Revenu Québec.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NEQ
First board resolution designating the tax depositary bank and authorized signatories
Proof of registered office address in Quebec
Beneficial ownership and director identification schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resubmit the BRO/Revenu Québec online application with corrected proof-of-identity documentation; access My Business Account and the Revenu Québec dashboard to complete any missing registration blocks; apply for retroactive account activation where necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Installation — Registered Office, Minute Book, Officer Appointments and Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Register of directors update; Corporation's registered office and corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational first board meeting or adopt unanimous written resolutions; adopt by-law No. 1; fix the registered office at the designated Quebec address; elect the President and Secretary-Treasurer; issue share certificates for the subscribed shares; prepare the securities register, register of directors and register of shareholders; file the notice of directors and prescribed update declaration with REQ within 60 days; complete the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and articles of incorporation
Approved by-law No. 1 (general corporate governance)
Notice of directors and officers update form (REQ register)
Share certificates and stock transfer ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure any omission by unanimous shareholder or board resolution; file a late declaration with REQ and CRA and pay the applicable late-filing penalty; appoint an interim officer by written resolution if a nominee declines to act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada — Consumer Product Safety Directorate (product safety); Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie du Québec (MEIE) (industrial promotion and manufacturing oversight); municipal authority issuing the establishment permit (permis d'exploitation)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Environmental Assessment and Authorization Service
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C — Registration / Declaration tier; full EIA report not mandated for light assembly of robotic toys (plastic injection moulding, electronic component insertion, battery charging); a ministerial registration under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment (REAFIE) is required when the establishment exceeds municipal industrial-activity thresholds; otherwise exemption with municipal approval.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the Règlement sur les rejets industriels dans les réseaux d'assainissement (CQLR c Q-2, r. 35) — pH 6.0 to 9.5, temperature ≤ 65°C, total suspended solids and heavy metals within municipal sewer limits; Air/VOCs: workplace VOC concentrations below Quebec occupational exposure limits; ensure battery-charging areas have mechanical ventilation certified under CNESST standards; Waste: electronics and lithium-battery waste handling per the Règlement sur la récupération et la valorisation de produits (RRPQ) and provincial hazardous-waste regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire safety service with structural load clearance under Chapter 1 of the National Building Code of Canada as adopted in Quebec (RBQ permit); workplace health-and-safety registration with CNESST including a hazard-prevention program, equipment electrical certification, and accessible-exit compliance; municipal zoning and noise attenuation clearance for light manufacturing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – GST/HST Program, Business Registration Online (BRO), My Business Account portal. Provincial (Quebec): Revenu Québec – Quebec Sales Tax (QST), payroll deductions and corporate income tax administration via Clic Revenu and the Registre des entreprises du Québec (REQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated corporation must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account from the CRA using Form RC148 (Non-Resident Registration) or Business Registration Online (BRO) before commencing commercial activity in Canada. In Quebec, the entity must also register with Revenu Québec under the System of Registration and the REQ, resulting in a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and a QST account number. Non-resident filers must appoint a Canadian representative with a completed Form RC391 (Power of Attorney) and maintain books and records in Canada or make them available electronically to the CRA and Revenu Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A Canadian business corporation is a separate legal taxpayer under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Taxation Act (Quebec). A resident Canadian corporation is subject to full Canadian tax on worldwide income, while a non-resident corporation is taxable only on Canadian-source business income attributable to a permanent establishment in Canada/Quebec. The provincial allocation follows Quebec's territorial sourcing and permanent establishment rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' entity classification election; a business corporation is per se a taxable Canadian corporation. Available statutory elections relevant to cross-border manufacturing/export entities include: (i) voluntarily registered GST/HST and QST elections to recover input tax credits on pre-operating and export-related expenses; (ii) the election under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act for nil consideration on supplies between closely related resident corporations (GST/HST neutralization); (iii) section 216 election (rental/royalty income) and section 217 election (Canadian pension benefits) for non-residents; and (iv) hybrid mismatch rules under sections 18.4-18.8 of the Income Tax Act (and Part 6.1) which neutralize double non-taxation arising from foreign entity classification mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) 5% federal VAT administered by the CRA combined with QST (Quebec Sales Tax) 9.975% provincial VAT administered by Revenu Québec. QST is computed on the selling price before GST, producing a combined consumer headline rate of 14.975% in Quebec. Manufacturing and export transactions are subject to the Excise Tax Act (Part IX) and the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax (CQLR c T-0.1).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: A supplier is a 'small supplier' and is not required to register for GST/HST or QST if its total worldwide/taxable supplies made in Canada in the current calendar quarter and the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters do not exceed CAD 30,000. Once the threshold is exceeded, registration with the CRA (GST/HST) and Revenu Québec (QST) is mandatory. Non-residents carrying on business in Canada are eligible for the same threshold; voluntary registration is available to recover input tax credits. Online marketplace and payment facilitator rules apply where sales are mediated through digital platforms.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, electronic invoicing, digital stamping, or tax-authority API validation regime for B2B/B2C supplies. The CRA participates in the voluntary Pan-Canadian Trust Framework / Peppol e-invoice standard, and Revenu Québec accepts structured electronic invoices, provided the prescribed invoice content is complete and legible. Corporations must e-file GST/HST and QST returns through the CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec portals; invoice data transmission to tax authorities is not required. Export invoices must show the supplier's BN/QST number, the zero-rated nature of the supply, and the foreign destination of the goods.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of tangible goods exported from Canada qualify for the 0% GST/HST rate under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act (and the mirror QST zero-rating provisions) when the supplier exports the goods before the supply, or delivers them to a common carrier for export, or the non-resident recipient exports the goods within the prescribed regulatory time limits. For the assembly of bionic robotic pet hardware (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930), the zero rating applies where possession is transferred in Canada and shipment is made to a destination outside Canada. Services performed directly on exported goods, and services supplied to non-residents not relating to Canadian real estate, are also zero-rated. The exporter must retain contemporaneous evidence of export, transport, payment and foreign destination; QST zero-rating follows the same documentary disciplines and the supplier must be a registered QST filer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: B13A Canada Customs Coding Form / Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) or G19 Non-Declaration Report filed with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) where shipment value exceeds CAD 2,000.

Transport and Commercial Documentation: Bill of Lading (ocean), Air Waybill (air), CIM/CMR consignment note (road/rail), commercial invoice and packing list showing the foreign consignee and exit port/terminal from Canada.

Inward Remittance / FX Repatriation Evidence: Bank SWIFT MT103, payment gateway settlement records, or foreign exchange conversion certificates demonstrating receipt of export proceeds from outside Canada within the commercial terms (benchmark period: 180 days).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess export zero-rating within the normal four-year limitation period, or beyond where misrepresentation, false statements, or fraud are established; unsubstantiated claims result in clawback of the GST/HST and QST input tax credits previously recovered in connection with exported goods, together with prescribed-rate interest. Civil penalties may range from 5% to 10% of the net tax misstatement for false or grossly negligent statements, plus a 50% gross negligence penalty under the Income Tax Act where income tax consequences are also adjusted. Failure to register penalties, suspension of QST registration, director's joint and several liability, and criminal prosecution for knowingly false documentation (including fines and imprisonment) may all be pursued. The 180-day FX repatriation benchmark serves primarily as an anti-avoidance and documentary substantiation threshold; commercial payment terms should be designed to repatriate export proceeds within that period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the monetary and clearing settlement authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential bank supervision; Department of Finance Canada as the statutory administrator of the Bank of Canada Act and the Payment Clearing and Settlement Act; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the AML/KYC supervisor. Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange control administration, reflecting the fully liberalized status of the Canadian dollar.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is unconditionally convertible on both current and capital account under the IMF Article VIII obligations; there are no surrender requirements and no differential treatment between residents and non-residents for deposit, borrowing, or remittance purposes. The only statutory gateways are the Investment Canada Act (net benefit review for foreign direct investment in Canada) and Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (generally 25% on dividend remittances unless reduced by treaty, e.g., 5% under the Canada-USA Treaty for qualified corporate shareholders). Profit remittance requires a valid board-drawn dividend resolution, Quebec corporate-law solvency certification, and a correctly executed Form NR601 if a waiver of the withholding obligation for treaty-reduced dividends is claimed. No prior Bank of Canada or Revenu Québec approval is necessary for the outward transfer of funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules in Canada. Exporters conducting the ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930 business (assembly of bionic companion robotic animals) are free to retain foreign currency receivables in domestic foreign-currency bank accounts or in offshore accounts without mandatory conversion into CAD. The only compliance obligations are: (i) accurate B13A declaration of exported goods to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for goods over CAD 2,000, with the reporting requirement met at the time of export; (ii) preserving underlying commercial invoices, bills of lading, and proof of receipt of payment for customs audit purposes; and (iii) the corporate requirement under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA) to render financial accounts in CAD while presenting foreign-currency translation in accordance with IFRS. No timeline, ratio, or conversion mandate applies to export receipts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium: Licenced offshore financial-tech EMIs (Wise Platform, Airwallex, Wex, and credas) may legally support cross-border disbursements into and out of Canada only as registered Payment Service Providers or Money Service Businesses under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) with registration with Bank of Canada, and where applicable FINTRAC MSB licensing. They cannot be treated as a primary bank for maintaining statutory share capital or dividend remittance because they do not hold deposit-taking licences; they are feasible for payment collection on the Stripe/card rails and for bilateral FX conversion of trade receivables. Legal constraints include the obligation to keep all settlement funds in a segregated trust account with a Canadian Schedule I bank, the impossibility of opening a FI (financial institution) deposit account in the fintech's own name, and the requirement to maintain beneficial-ownership transparency with FINTRAC under PCMLTFA Part 1. The recommended architecture is a Tier-1 domestic bank account as the legal treasury anchor, with the fintech EMT used only for merchant-led fund routing and low-value B2B supplier payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Federally regulated Canadian banks and Desjardins are not prohibited from opening corporate accounts remotely. FINTRAC recognizes both face-to-face and non-face-to-face identity verification under Section 64 of the PCMLTFA Regulations, provided that a reliable, independent, source-of-truth document is obtained (e.g., an authenticated passport with video-link confirmation). The default expectation for a Quebec-incorporated entity with non-resident shareholders and foreign directors is that the following must occur at account opening: (i) at least one director or officer, usually the authorized signatory, completes a bank-mandated digital video interview; (ii) the beneficial-ownership declaration under FINTRAC Rule s. 71 is attested in writing; (iii) the statutory Beneficial Ownership Register is filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) prior to the opening; and (iv) Canadian anti-money-laundering enhanced due diligence (EDD) is applied because of the foreign-source capital contribution. Physical attendance at a Canadian branch is not statutorily compulsory, but its absence materially raises onboarding turnaround time to 10-14 business days. For the most efficient closure, the account signer should be physically present at an NBC or RBC branch in Montreal, Quebec during the corporate setup trip.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contribution denominated in USD or CNY exceeding CAD 250,000 from a non-resident shareholder with no visible operating revenue connectivity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Notarized Certificate of Incorporation (QBCA) and REQ attestation; (2) Fully executed shareholders' agreement and capital subscription resolution; (3) Clarified source-of-wealth statement of the shareholder including audited financial statements, estate tax proof, or sale-of-company closing letters; (4) Board resolution itemizing the capital injection, the settlement account, and the projected deployment for inventory of robotic components; (5) Bank statement of the transferee and SWIFT MT103 reference evidencing the value date; (6) Pre-confirmed Business Number (BN) from Canada Revenue Agency and PST/QST registration certificate from Revenu Québec to demonstrate expected commercial activity; (7) Signed representation letter confirming no MSB status and no tokenization of the AI pet robot.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment pattern with high-volume low-value inbound settlement from Stripe/card acquirers intermingled with outbound payments to volumetric suppliers in China, conflicting with the declared toy-hardware manufacturing model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Stripe master merchant agreement and settlement schedule describing the card-issuing mandate; (2) Itemized receivables ledger matched to the ISIC 3240 business description, including product stock-keeping-unit (SKU) list and sales invoices; (3) Signed supplier agreements, commercial invoices, and the full purchase order trail from the component vendor in East Asia, each corroborated by customs B13A export declarations from CBSA; (4) Inventory-movement evidence including sea/air waybill and receipt-in-warehouse records in Quebec, demonstrating physical movement of bionic animal components; (5) Updated cash-flow forecast identifying the proportion of proceeds that will be cleared to third-party suppliers, proving that the account is operational rather than a pass-through.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Quebec Beneficial-Ownership Registry (REQ) non-compliance: non-resident shareholder holding 25% or more of the corporation has not been declared, and the bank's CDD software automatically flags the account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Executed Quebec Registered Beneficial Ownership filing confirmation (form REQ-BU) dated within 15 days of any ownership change, evidencing the name, date of birth, address, and control percentage of every UBO; (2) Copy of the 'Registre des bénéficiaires ultimes' extract provided by the Registraire des entreprises; (3) A board-certified list of ultimate owners covering the round of financing under which the capital was remitted; (4) Notarized privacy waiver allowing the bank to release the REQ filing to FINTRAC; (5) Proof of the non-resident's no-objection to tax-evasion scrutiny, including the CRS reporting certificate from the Canadian financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Artificial intelligence hardware exports with embedded speech synthesizers being proposed for restricted jurisdictions or with cyber-surveillance componentry tripping Canadian Controlled Goods and Export Control List (EGL) screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Full Technical Data Package of the AI pet robot demonstrating that the speech synthesizer and robotic assembly are consumer-companion grade and do not contain Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) category A/B items; (2) signed Written Confirmation of Non-Foreign-Affiliation or Controlled Goods Incident screening letter where applicable, or, if ineligible, an approved CGP registration; (3) ITAR-free / EGL-free attestation from the component supplier and the applicable HS classification (HS 9503 / 8543); (4) End-User Certificate and End-Use Statement for any robotics hardware movement; (5) KYC declaration confirming no sale to the Restricted and Sanctioned Country list maintained by Global Affairs Canada.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Accept only wire transfers in CAD or convert at a Tier-1 bank's treasury desk; mandated USD/CNY transfers must be routed via clearing SWIFT MT103 to the Toronto or Montreal correspondent and then converted at or near the Bank of Canada daily reference rate with a fixed FX confirmation order. The wire message must state a purpose code of 'G20' (equity contribution) or 'G55' (intercompany direct investment) as recognized by the Bank of Canada's balance-of-payments account; the remitter must align the SWIFT tag 50F with the non-resident shareholder's legal name exactly as registered in the REQ registry. The Quebec corporation must issue a director resolution designating that all inbound capital is held in a zoned 'Capital Proceeds Account' exclusively for future operations, and the account holder must apply a two-step approval for any debit within 30 days of receipt. For capital above CAD 1 million, the bank must be notified 3 business days in advance and the corporate treasury must produce an internal verification call to the kyc officer to avoid a regulatory hold under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for imported bionic robot componentry, offshore tooling, and licensing royalties should be executed via: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier transfers under USD/CNY, containing the beneficiary branch address in China and the corresponding application of Incoterms 2020 (CIF or FOB) as documented in the purchase order; (2) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (LC) under Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600) with a Canadian confirming bank, available by sight payment, covering raw material imports above CAD 250,000; the LC must specify a marine/ocean bill of lading issued to the order of the Quebec corporation and may include a certificate of the robotic assembly's ISIC 3240 classification to satisfy trade-based money laundering review; (3) the Canadian High-Value Clearing System (Lynx, formerly LVTS) for JIT supplier disbursements within Canada, which settles irrevocably on the same-value day; and (4) continuous SWIFT gpi tracking for any payment exceeding CAD 100,000, with mandatory six-year archival of the MT103, LC, invoices, and customs B3 declarants under PCMLTFA record-keeping. For all USD-denominated outflows, the bank will require the corporate taxpayer to confirm the underlying trade evidence in an electronic document repository, thus preventing the account from being characterized as a pass-through treasury.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright CAD/USD Foreign Exchange Forwards: Deliverable forward contracts with any Canadian Schedule I bank under a bilateral ISDA Master Agreement or bank-standard FX Master Agreement (FXMAP), permitted without clearing obligation if the notional is below the $10 billion threshold for FX forwards excluded from mandatory clearing under the Canadian Derivatives Act regime.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): Permissible in CAD/CNY and CAD/RMB where the underlying trade obligations are invoiced in CNY, subject to the bank's own credit approval and documentation of the non-transferability ruling of the People's Bank of China for the specific settlement date; the corporate must maintain the interbank statement evidencing the NDF reference rate.

Cross-Currency Swaps (FX Swaps / Basis Swaps): Available for rolling CAD/USD funding positions at the corporate treasury level, with the swap embedded in a standard ISDA 2002 or the bank's FX Basis Swap Master Agreement; the instrument is explicitly recognized under the Bank of Canada's Payment Clearing and Settlement Act as an eligible financial contract not requiring registration with a clearing house.

At-The-Money and European-Style FX Options: Permitted only with a classification of 'end-user' if the hedging is directly related to the commercial resale of robotic units and the net notional across all instruments does not exceed the projected 18-month trade exposure; the corporation must file the quarterly Derivatives Reporting Form T-1/D-1 with OED (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) if the gross notional of all commodity and FX derivatives exceeds the CAD 10 billion threshold, which is not expected at this launch scale.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director of Corporations, Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years permits administrative dissolution by Corporations Canada; a CAD 100 late filing fee applies to overdue annual returns, and revival requires payment of arrears and filing the overdue returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the enterprise's registration in the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing exposes the enterprise to a REQ notice, administrative cancellation of registration, and loss of legal capacity to transact until the registration is reinstated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeat non-filing attracts a 10% penalty, and daily compound interest accrues on unpaid balances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each taxation year, concurrently with the federal T2 return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and interest are imposed under the Taxation Act; continued default may result in arbitrary assessment, enforced collection, and director liability for unremitted source deductions or corporate tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based statutory audit threshold applies to this private CBCA/QBCA corporation. A mandatory independent audit is required only if the corporation is a distributing or reporting issuer, or if the shareholders do not unanimously waive auditor appointment; a non-offering corporation may renew the waiver annually by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP under the CPA Canada Handbook; reporting issuers must use IFRS (Part I), while private enterprises may elect to use Canadian ASPE (Part II) or IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: If formed under the CBCA, the corporation must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC), update it within 15 days of any share transfer or change in significant control, and confirm ISC information when filing the federal annual return. For a Quebec provincial corporation, share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the REQ annual declaration where director, officer, or controlling shareholder particulars change; no separate Quebec-wide UBO declaration is otherwise required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (organizational, annual, and special resolutions)
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) (federal CBCA corporations)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 150–500 (approximate USD equivalent of CAD 200–650 per year)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000–25,000 (approximate USD equivalent of CAD 7,000–35,000 per engagement); nil if the audit is waived by unanimous shareholder consent
